newsitem.title: USA: Leaking dikes prompt emergency action in Fargo.
newsitem.headline: Leaking dikes prompt emergency action in Fargo.

text.p: Hundreds of volunteers worked feverishly overnight and into Wednesday morning as earthern dikes sprang leaks while the Red River continued rising, reaching an unprecedented 38.55 feet.

A 6-foot dike was under construction along 4-1/2 blocks of downtown Fargo in case the primary dike gives way, Dennis Walaker, operations manager for Fargo's public works, said. "Sandbagging efforts went on all night," he said. "A lot of the sandbagged areas need shoring up."

The Red River, gorged with runoff from a record winter snowfall in the northern plains, was rising about 1/4-inch-an hour Wednesday, down from from Tuesday's 1/2-inch hourly rise. Wallaker said it may crest Thursday morning at about 38.8 feet, more than 20 feet over flood level.
North Dakota State University closed Wednesday to allow students, faculty and staff to join the emergency efforts.
Flooding has forced the evacuation of many small cities and rural areas along the Red River and its tributaries.

In Grand Forks, N.D., about 75 miles downstream from Fargo, the Red was at 47.5 feet Wednesday and city officials have plans to evacuate low lying areas when the river reaches its expected 50-foot crest this weekend, Byron Sieber, spokesman for the city's Emergency Operations Centre, said.

Two of three bridges connecting the city to East Grand Forks, Minn., have been closed and the third was threatened. Sieber said every effort will be made to keep open the third bridge, which should withstand a 50-foot river level.
"We would be doing the diking at the landings on each end of the bridge," he said.

The United States Coast Guard conducted helicopter surveys north of Fargo Tuesday but no rescues of flood-stranded residents were necessary, Chief Warrant Officer Randy Caverly at the Coast Guard's Fargo office said.
Earlier this week, residents, their willpower drained by nearly a week of being surrounded by high water, appealed to the Coast Guard and emergency crews to be rescued.
